# `lunar-orbit-rendezvous`

Scenario kind of the engine v0.39.0, family [Lunar and cislunar](../lunar-and-cislunar.md). Advisory: analysis output from a research and engineering tool, not type-approved navigation equipment and not a safety-of-life service. Every label here is the engine's or the verification matrix's; a kind is MODELLED unless the matrix says otherwise (how a label is earned: the README's Evidence section).

## What it does

MODELLED relative navigation for an Orion-lander style docking in a low lunar orbit or an elliptical polar orbit (Artemis-class). A chaser and a target fly the same orbit under the crate's lunar force model; a joint 21-parameter batch Gauss-Newton estimate over the arc (two vehicle states and persistent signal-in-space biases) fuses an absolute position fix per vehicle from an ILLUSTRATIVE LCNS-class relay set (relays behind the Moon dropped, four needed, the common-mode signal-in-space error cancelling between the vehicles) and a crosslink range, with ranging precision from the code-tracking bound on the LunaNet AFS pilot. Reports the formal and Monte Carlo relative position and velocity error in the target LVLH axes, fix availability, the mean normalised estimation error squared against its expected value, and any trial whose iteration did not converge, the drift from ignoring the gravity harmonics, and the full 6x6 covariance handed on. A closed-form Hill/Clohessy-Wiltshire check applies to the circular case. MODELLED: illustrative relay set, error budget and priors; the truth and the estimator share one force model, so the NEES checks self-consistency and not model error. Not agency-endorsed; advisory software, not certified navigation equipment.

One run of `scenarios/lunar-orbit-rendezvous.toml` summarises as: lunar-orbit-rendezvous | llo 100x100 km | sep 2000 m | fixes 74% | rel pos 1-sigma R/A/C 0.03/0.06/0.04 m | mean NEES 6.51 (6 expected) | converged at 2000 s (MODELLED)
